items.prompt:
Energy and fuels people use come from
A) natural resources
B) nowhere
C) only batteries
D) only the Moon

steps: Energy and fuels come from Earth's natural resources.

items.prompt:
Which is a fossil fuel?
A) Sunlight
B) Coal
C) Wind
D) Moving water

Fossil fuels are
A) renewable
B) non-renewable
C) made of sunlight
D) never used

steps: Fossil fuels can run out, so they are non-renewable.

items.prompt:
Which is a renewable energy resource?
A) Coal
B) Oil
C) Sunlight
D) Natural gas

steps: Solar, wind, and water power are renewable.

items.prompt:
Compared with burning coal, solar power usually
A) pollutes more
B) pollutes less
C) pollutes the same
D) uses more coal

steps: Solar power generally causes less pollution than coal.

items.prompt:
Non-renewable means the resource
A) is never used
B) can run out
C) is made of sunlight
D) grows back fast

steps: Non-renewable resources are used up and can run out.

items.prompt:
Burning fossil fuels for a city's electricity can
A) clean the air
B) release pollution into the air
C) make the Sun brighter
D) create new coal
items.answer: B) release pollution into the air

steps: Burning fossil fuels pollutes the air.

items.prompt:
Why combine information from more than one source about energy?
A) To waste time
B) To get a fuller, more complete picture
C) To hide facts
D) There is no reason
items.answer: B) To get a fuller, more complete picture

steps: Combining sources gives more complete information.
